practices.name: TRT without a prescription
practices.claim: Self-sourced testosterone, with no doctor and no blood work, is a safe shortcut for healthy men to build muscle, drive and a more masculine look.
practices.evidence_rationale: Testosterone therapy has mostly been tested in men with symptoms and repeatedly low blood levels; one short randomized trial in healthy men with normal levels found larger muscles and more strength at above-normal exposure, especially alongside training, but it aimed at muscle outcomes and says little about long-term safety, so the 'safe shortcut' claim has no direct support. The Endocrine Society guideline limits treatment to men with deficiency symptoms plus unequivocally and consistently low results.
practices.risk_rationale: Without blood work or monitoring, users cannot know their baseline or catch blood-pressure, blood-thickness or fertility problems, and a systematic review found about a third of black-market anabolic steroid samples were counterfeit and a similar share substandard. Even under supervision, the largest trial, in men aged 45-80 with low testosterone and heart disease or a high risk of it, saw more atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism and kidney injury than placebo, so treatment needs monitoring.
key_harms: Reduced fertility
Higher blood pressure and thicker blood
Atrial fibrillation, clots and kidney injury (trial signal)
Counterfeit or mislabeled products
practices.safer_alternative: See a GP or endocrinologist for repeat morning blood tests and a proper work-up before any hormone treatment. If levels are normal, sleep, resistance training and body-fat management are the routes with evidence; if fertility matters, raise it before starting anything.

legal_status.US: Schedule III controlled substance (anabolic steroids) under DEA scheduling.
legal_status.UK: Class C controlled drug (Schedule 4 Part II); supply requires authorisation.
legal_status.CA: Anabolic steroids are Schedule IV controlled substances under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act.

practices.name: SARMs
practices.claim: SARMs deliver steroid-like muscle gain and fat loss without the side effects of steroids.
practices.evidence_rationale: Randomized trials, mostly in older and clinical populations, show a modest gain in lean mass and physical performance, not steroid-like changes in healthy young men. Nothing supports the 'no side effects' half of the claim, and reviews of recreational users report drug-induced liver injury.
practices.risk_rationale: FDA and Health Canada say SARMs are unapproved drugs linked to liver injury and possible heart-attack and stroke risk. Lab testing of products sold online as SARMs found that only 41% matched their label for the active compound and 39% contained other unapproved drugs.
key_harms: Drug-induced liver injury
Lower HDL cholesterol and suppressed natural testosterone
Possible heart attack or stroke (FDA warning)
Mislabeled products with undeclared drugs
practices.safer_alternative: Progressive resistance training with adequate protein and sleep; creatine monohydrate is the supplement with strong evidence. If you suspect a hormone problem, an endocrinologist can test and treat it properly.

legal_status.US: Unapproved drugs; FDA states they cannot be legally marketed as a drug or a dietary supplement.
legal_status.CA: Not authorized in Canada for any medical use.

practices.name: DNP
practices.claim: DNP strips body fat fast, giving a quick route to a leaner, more defined physique.
practices.evidence_rationale: Reviews report rapid weight loss with DNP, which was used as a weight-loss drug before the US declared it not fit for human consumption in 1938, but this rests on historical and uncontrolled reports and no modern controlled trials were found. The weight loss comes with severe, sometimes fatal toxicity.
practices.risk_rationale: DNP drives the body to overheat, there is no specific antidote, and a medical review counted 62 published deaths. A UK poison-service series recorded five deaths among 23 reported toxic exposures, mostly in young men.
key_harms: Fatal overheating with no specific antidote
Documented deaths in the UK, Australia and elsewhere
Cataracts and liver damage (FDA)
Rapid heart rate, fever, sweating and collapse
practices.safer_alternative: Supervised weight-loss care from a doctor or registered dietitian, which can include approved medication where it is clinically indicated.

legal_status.US: FDA has never approved DNP for human consumption.
legal_status.UK: Not treated as a controlled drug; the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs advises that it is a poison rather than a drug, and Public Health England has said it is unfit for human consumption.

practices.name: GLP-1 agonists from non-pharmacy sources
practices.claim: GLP-1 weight-loss injections bought outside regulated pharmacies give the same large, fast fat loss as prescribed ones, for less money.
practices.evidence_rationale: Randomized trials show that prescribed, regulated GLP-1 treatment produces substantial weight loss, but none test products bought outside pharmacies. One small product-testing study of such sellers judged every sample probable substandard or falsified, so equivalence is unproven.
practices.risk_rationale: Regulators in the US and UK warn of counterfeit, contaminated or mislabeled products, and the UK saw hospitalisations after fake pens that appeared to contain insulin. A product-testing study found very low purity and endotoxin in every sample, while supervised use scores 2 because it is prescription-only with common gastrointestinal side effects.
key_harms: Low blood sugar and coma from fakes that appeared to contain insulin
Contamination, including endotoxin, and injection infections
Wrong-strength or mislabeled products serious enough to need hospital care
Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea (common even with approved use)
practices.safer_alternative: Get a prescription from a licensed clinician and fill it at a licensed pharmacy. If cost is the barrier, ask the prescriber about other approved options and structured lifestyle programmes.

legal_status.US: Prescription-only; FDA warns that unapproved or counterfeit versions have not been reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality.
legal_status.UK: Prescription-only medicines; only registered pharmacies may legally supply them.

practices.name: Research peptides (e.g. BPC-157)
practices.claim: Injectable 'research' peptides such as BPC-157 speed up healing of tendons, muscles and gut injuries and improve recovery.
practices.evidence_rationale: A 2025 systematic review found 36 studies on BPC-157 in orthopaedic sports medicine, 35 of them preclinical and one a small uncontrolled series of 12 patients with knee pain. No controlled human trial was among them.
practices.risk_rationale: The same review found no clinical safety data, and FDA has said it lacks enough information to know whether BPC-157 would harm people, citing immunogenicity concerns. Health Canada adds that unauthorized injectable peptides may contain wrong amounts or contaminants whatever the 'research use only' label says.
key_harms: No human safety data
Immune reactions (immunogenicity risk flagged by FDA)
Infection or allergic reaction from injected, unregulated product
Wrong or contaminated contents
practices.safer_alternative: For a stubborn injury, see a sports-medicine physician or physiotherapist for a diagnosis and a supervised loading-based rehabilitation plan. For gut symptoms, see a GP or gastroenterologist.

legal_status.US: FDA's briefing document for the July 2026 advisory committee meeting proposed that BPC-157 not be included on the pharmacy-compounding bulks list (ulcerative colitis use); the committee is advisory only, and no final FDA determination has been published.
legal_status.CA: Unauthorized; Health Canada says 'research use only' labelling gives no exemption from the rules.

practices.name: Creatine monohydrate
practices.claim: Creatine monohydrate reliably adds strength and lean mass and is safe for healthy men.
practices.evidence_rationale: A 2024 meta-analysis of randomized trials in adults under 50 found creatine plus resistance training raised upper- and lower-body strength more than placebo, with larger effects in men. The ISSN position stand and a 2025 meta-analysis of kidney outcomes support its safety in healthy people.
practices.risk_rationale: Weight gain is the only side effect consistently reported in healthy users. A 2025 meta-analysis found a small rise in blood creatinine but no change in kidney filtration.
key_harms: Weight gain
Small rise in blood creatinine with no change in kidney filtration

legal_status.US: FDA completed a 2020 review of a GRAS notice for creatine monohydrate as an ingredient in certain foods and drinks and had no questions.

proposed.name: Clomiphene / enclomiphene as a 'natural TRT' alternative
proposed.why: It is a recurring community claim that sits between prescribed TRT and SARMs, so readers comparing those options will look for it. It needs its own claim, evidence and risk grading rather than being folded into the TRT entry.
